$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

The marginal mass functions of the independent discrete random variables X and Y are shown below. Given that the corresponding joint probability mass function is f(x,y), find f(2,5).

x 2 4 6
fX(x) 0.2 0.6 0.2

y 1 3 5
fY(y) 0.1 0.4 0.5
a
0.24
b
0.1
c
0.3
d
Impossible to determine using the given information.
e
0.08
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Two discrete random variables X and Y with joint probability mass function f(x,y) are independent if and only if f(x,y)=fX(x)⋅fY(y) for all possible values x and y, where fX(x) and fY(y) are the marginal probability mass functions for X and Y, respectively.

Therefore, since our discrete random variables are independent, we obtain f(2,5)=fX(2)⋅fY(5)=0.2⋅0.5=0.1.

q-162900.name: Question 15
q-162900.problem:
The partially complete joint probability distribution $f(x,y)$ of the independent discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is below. 

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=5$ | $0.12$ | $∗$ | $?$ |
| $X=7$ | $0.24$ | $∗$ | $∗$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.36$ | $0.64$ | $1$ |

What is the value of $P(X=5)?$
q-162900.worked_solution:
Two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with a joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Therefore, since our random variables are independent, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5,0) & ={f}_{X}(5)\cdot {f}_{Y}(0) \\ P(X=5,Y=0) & =P(X=5)\cdot P(Y=0) \\ 0.12 & =P(X=5)\cdot 0.36 \\ P(X=5) & =\frac{0.12}{0.36} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
